title: Gaza Ministry of Health: 72,939 Killed, 172,927 Wounded Since October 7, 2023; 930 Killed Since Ceasefire
detail: Gaza's Ministry of Health issued updated cumulative figures on May 31, 2026: 72,939 Palestinians killed and 172,927 wounded since October 7, 2023. The figures cover only those who reached hospitals and represent a lower bound, as thousands remain missing under rubble in inaccessible areas — with 781 additional bodies recovered from rubble since the October 2025 ceasefire. Since the ceasefire went into effect on October 11, 2025, 930 Palestinians have been killed and 2,819 wounded by Israeli strikes — described by Gaza's Government Media Office as 3,005+ ceasefire violations. The UN has confirmed the continuation of a famine emergency in Gaza, with WFP's IPC Phase 5 designation covering the Gaza governorate. By end of June 2026, an estimated 43,400 children face severe risk of death from malnutrition — triple the January 2026 estimate. Only 49,973 of 135,600 allocated aid trucks entered Gaza from October 2025 to May 27, 2026 — just 36% of the required volume.

media.caption: Gaza Health Ministry: 72,939 killed, 172,927 wounded since Oct 7 — May 31, 2026

title: ICJ Confirms Written Pleadings Schedule in South Africa v. Israel Genocide Case
detail: The International Court of Justice confirmed the written pleadings schedule for South Africa v. Israel (Case No. 192, Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide). By order of May 21, 2026, the ICJ directed: South Africa to file its Reply by November 22, 2027; Israel to file its Rejoinder by May 22, 2029. The case is now progressing through written pleadings after Israel filed its counter-memorial on March 12, 2026. Interveners in the case as of May 2026 include Namibia, the United States, Hungary, Fiji, the Netherlands, and Iceland. Germany withdrew from Israel's side to prepare for its own ICJ case. The extended timeline means a final ICJ ruling on the merits is unlikely before 2030. The ICJ issued provisional measures in January 2024 ordering Israel to prevent acts of genocide but stopping short of ordering a ceasefire.

media.caption: ICJ confirms written pleadings schedule in South Africa v. Israel genocide case — Case 192

title: Colombia Election Outcome to Determine Future of Israel Diplomatic Relations
detail: Colombia's presidential election on May 31, 2026 carried significant implications for Israel. Under President Gustavo Petro, Colombia severed diplomatic ties with Israel in May 2024 — one of the most high-profile breaks with Israel by a Latin American country during the Gaza war. Petro, who leaves office in 2026, had been among the most vocal global critics of Israeli military operations, repeatedly using genocide terminology. The election outcome will determine whether Colombia restores relations with Israel under a more moderate successor, maintains the break, or deepens it. South Korea President Lee Jae Myung, meanwhile, called Netanyahu a 'war criminal' in May 2026 and ordered evaluation of whether to issue an arrest warrant in line with the ICC. The accumulation of diplomatic breaks and ICC-compliance pressure has increasingly constrained Netanyahu's diplomatic travel options.

media.caption: Colombia election on May 31 to determine future of Israel diplomatic relations after 2024 break

title: Gaza's Government Media Office Counts 3,005 Israeli Ceasefire Violations Since October 2025
detail: Gaza's Government Media Office documented 3,005 Israeli violations of the October 2025 ceasefire as of May 27, 2026, including 1,109 airstrikes and shelling attacks and 921 shootings targeting civilians. The violations include targeted killings of Hamas commanders — two successive Qassam Brigades chiefs killed in May — as well as strikes on police posts, displacement camps, markets, healthcare workers, and civilian infrastructure. Ceasefire implementation overseer Nickolay Mladenov (former Bulgarian FM) warned the UN Security Council that without progress toward Phase 2, Gaza faces indefinite crisis. Phase 2, which would lead to a permanent end to the war, is stalled over Hamas's rejection of a disarmament framework presented by the US-led Board of Peace in March 2026 as 'unacceptable.' Hamas has warned the ceasefire faces collapse following Israeli escalations including the May 26 strike on the Tel al-Sultan displacement camp and the targeted killing of civilian doctors and police.

media.caption: Seven months into the Gaza ceasefire: 3,005 Israeli violations documented — Middle East Eye
